correctness.rationale: The proof reduces extensions of a partial perfect matching to derangement completions on the omitted indices. The two-index case has exactly one alternative swap, and the at-least-three case always has a second completion by a nonadjacent swap or inversion of a \(3\)-cycle. The count \(n-t_2(\pi)\) follows from the undirected cycle graph. Exhaustive direct extension counting for \(3\le n\le8\) independently verifies 4,053,088 subset instances and all stated coefficients.

originality.rationale: The scalar minimum forcing number is treated as covered by later general bipartite results and is not the originality basis. The retained result classifies every forcing subset of every crown perfect matching and finds a cycle-type-sensitive minimum-set count and aggregate enumerator. Targeted alias searches, database searches, the 2011 forcing survey, the 2015 forcing-polynomial paper, and the 2021 broad forcing-number paper did not supply or imply this all-subset statement.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper may use a nonstandard name for crown graphs and explicitly count forcing subsets rather than only forcing numbers.
The all-subset enumerator Phi_pi is a natural refinement but is not the same established invariant as the standard forcing polynomial; terminology must remain explicit.
The 1985 book-chapter precursor was identified historically but not assigned an exact public day; the package uses the later exact-day 1987 source without inventing a 1985 date.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete structural classification of a core set system in perfect-matching forcing theory. It explains why the standard forcing polynomial loses all cycle-type information on crowns, then recovers an exact matching-sensitive statistic \(n-t_2(\pi)\) and an aggregate derangement formula. This is mathematically natural and not an arbitrary parameter slice.
